an3.62:1.1: “Monks, uneducated run-of-the-mill people describe three things as mother-&-child-separating dangers.
an3.62:1.3: “There comes a time when a great fire-conflagration breaks out.
an3.62:1.4: When a great fire-conflagration breaks out, it burns villages, towns, & cities.
an3.62:1.5: When it is burning villages, towns, & cities, a mother there can’t get to her child, and the child can’t get to its mother.
an3.62:1.6: This is the first thing that uneducated run-of-the-mill people describe as a mother-&-child-separating danger.
an3.62:2.1: “Then again there comes a time when a great cloud arises.
an3.62:2.2: When a great cloud arises, a great flood of water is produced.
an3.62:2.3: When a great flood of water is produced, it floods villages, towns, & cities.
an3.62:2.4: When it is flooding villages, towns, & cities, a mother there can’t get to her child, and the child can’t get to its mother.
an3.62:2.5: This is the second thing that uneducated run-of-the-mill people describe as a mother-&-child-separating danger.
an3.62:3.1: “Then again there comes a time when there is danger and an invasion of savage tribes. Taking power, they surround the countryside.
an3.62:3.2: When this happens, a mother there can’t get to her child, and the child can’t get to its mother.
an3.62:3.3: This is the third thing that uneducated run-of-the-mill people describe as a mother-&-child-separating danger.
an3.62:3.4: “These are the three things that uneducated run-of-the-mill people describe as mother-&-child-separating dangers.
an3.62:4.1: “But there are these three things that are mother-&-child-uniting dangers, yet run-of-the-mill people describe them as mother-&-child-separating dangers.
an3.62:4.3: “There comes a time when a great fire-conflagration breaks out.
an3.62:4.4: When a great fire-conflagration breaks out, it burns villages, towns, & cities.
an3.62:4.5: When it is burning villages, towns, & cities, there are times when it so happens that a mother can get to her child, and the child can get to its mother.
an3.62:4.6: This is the first thing that is a mother-&-child-uniting danger, yet run-of-the-mill people describe it as a mother-&-child-separating danger.
an3.62:5.1: “Then again there comes a time when a great cloud arises.
an3.62:5.2: When a great cloud arises, a great flood of water is produced.
an3.62:5.3: When a great flood of water is produced, it floods villages, towns, & cities.
an3.62:5.4: When it is flooding villages, towns, & cities, there are times when it so happens that a mother can get to her child, and the child can get to its mother.
an3.62:5.5: This is the second thing that is a mother-&-child-uniting danger, yet run-of-the-mill people describe it as a mother-&-child-separating danger.
an3.62:6.1: “Then again there comes a time when there is danger and an invasion of savage tribes. Taking power, they surround the countryside.
an3.62:6.2: When this happens, there are times when it so happens that a mother can get to her child, and the child can get to its mother.
an3.62:6.3: This is the third thing that is a mother-&-child-uniting danger, yet run-of-the-mill people describe it as a mother-&-child-separating danger.
an3.62:6.4: “These are the three things that are mother-&-child-uniting dangers, yet run-of-the-mill people describe them as mother-&-child-separating dangers.
an3.62:7.1: “There are these three things that are (genuine) mother-&-child-separating dangers.
an3.62:7.3: The danger of aging, the danger of illness, the danger of death.
an3.62:7.4: “A mother can’t get (her wish) with regard to her child who is aging,
an3.62:7.5: ‘I am aging, but may my child not age.’
an3.62:7.6: A child can’t get (its wish) with regard to its mother who is aging,
an3.62:7.7: ‘I am aging, but may my mother not age.’
an3.62:8.1: “A mother can’t get (her wish) with regard to her child who is growing ill,
an3.62:8.2: ‘I am growing ill, but may my child not grow ill.’
an3.62:8.3: A child can’t get (its wish) with regard to its mother who is growing ill,
an3.62:8.4: ‘I am growing ill, but may my mother not grow ill.’
an3.62:9.1: “A mother can’t get (her wish) with regard to her child who is dying,
an3.62:9.2: ‘I am dying, but may my child not die.’
an3.62:9.3: A child can’t get (its wish) with regard to its mother who is dying,
an3.62:9.4: ‘I am dying, but may my mother not die.’
an3.62:9.5: “These are the three things that are (genuine) mother-&-child-separating dangers.
an3.62:10.1: “There is a path, there is a practice, that leads to the abandoning and overcoming of these three mother-&-child-uniting dangers and these three mother-&-child-separating dangers.
an3.62:10.2: “And which is that path, which is that practice…?
an3.62:10.3: Just this very noble eightfold path, i.e.,
an3.62:10.4: right view, right resolve, right speech, right action, right livelihood, right effort, right mindfulness, right concentration.
an3.62:10.5: “This is the path, this the practice, that leads to the abandoning and overcoming of these three mother-&-child-uniting dangers and these three mother-&-child-separating dangers.”
